title: Grateful Dead Live at Hollywood Palladium on 1972-09-09
lineage: CD -> Cool Edit Pro v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with good clarity (minor drop‑outs) captures a high‑energy 1972 show highlighted by stellar Jack Straw, Friend of the Devil, The Other One and Stella Blue.
ai_review.review: The Miller soundboard tape delivers mostly clear audio despite a few scattered drop‑outs, letting the band’s strong performance shine. Highlights include an excellent Jack Straw, a tight Friend of the Devil played at its original tempo, a soaring The Other One, and Jerry’s clean vocal on Stella Blue. Even without Pigpen, the show “smokes” thanks to inventive guitar/piano ad‑libs and Bob’s playful lyric twist in Me and My Uncle.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently positive reviews (4–5 stars) praise both the musical performance and recording quality; minor technical glitches are noted but do not detract from overall enjoyment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced sound; a few drop‑outs reported on Disc One, likely due to the copy source. One reviewer notes “good sound from a cassette tape,” indicating the original board quality is solid.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Competent and well‑structured set despite Pigpen’s absence; songs flow smoothly with notable instrumental ad‑libs in the middle of the show.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Clean vocal tone on Stella Blue and strong guitar work, especially during improvisational sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Alternate lyric twist heard in Me and My Uncle, showing his playful vocal contributions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux praised for piano/keyboard ad‑libs and overall competent playing throughout the show.
